Saved history could escape suppression after row A passed its check while row B awaited. A whole-response retention fence now holds every subject's shared transition lock through final membership/Core authorization and synchronous construction of the exact bounded response bytes. Suppression takes the matching exclusive lock before its ledger append. Another sequential recheck cannot satisfy this guarantee.

This PR also retains the reviewed continuation repair: an already committed naturally completed/failed successor is read back only through its persisted exact continuation control. Existing mail, memory, Stop, selected-output and DOCX/XLSX repairs were reviewed rather than duplicated.

## Follow-up behavior

- Acquire sorted/deduplicated page subject locks on one PostgreSQL lease; keep canonical watermark/current-ledger recovery checks.
- Propagate the internal fence deadline/cancellation through publication, so delayed authorization cannot publish after lock retirement.
- Require successful release-phase native membership before publication and serialize measured response bytes once.
- Withhold transcript/list/next-turn receipts when Core archives during final membership; preserve `RESULT_NOT_RELEASED` and no repeated admission.
- The exact old-source A/B regression fails because suppression acknowledges while B awaits; the repaired path holds that suppression until response construction.

Stacked on PR179 `141f2ada`; PR175 remains unchanged at `993f52a9`.

## Passing focused checks

- Final root backend follow-up: **123/123 across eight files**, no skips.
- Independent final release-fence file: **18/18** (overlapping).
- Source syntax, both affected provenance generators/checks and source/Markdown/JSON whitespace pass.
- Paired [frontend PR98](https://github.com/neo-capiro/capiro-frontend/pull/98): **69/69 units**, **14/14 browser tests**, final strengthened cross-run cases **2/2** (overlapping), TypeScript, scoped lint/format/architecture and **283/283-page** production build pass.
- The earlier 585/585 run belongs to the initial PR180 checkpoint and is labeled separately in the report.

## Remaining failures — standard release gates remain red

Fresh identical-environment parent/current comparison:

| Check | PR179 parent | Initial and repaired PR180 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard tests | 4,356 passed / 33 failed / 4,389 | 4,357 passed / **32 failed** / 4,389 |
| Runtime TypeScript | 3 diagnostics | Same 3, byte-identical |
| Control TypeScript | 18 diagnostics | Same 18, byte-identical |

Every one of the 32 failing test names, assertions, declaration locations, expected/actual errors and individual classifications is in the [exact inventory](https://github.com/neo-capiro/meri-greenfield/blob/a1876afaeaa59d9da47729487d490cba8cfc9d9c/docs/integration/audit-evidence-20261018/FAILURE-BASELINE-INVENTORY.md), with full scrubbed historical/parent/current/post-fix logs, commands and hashes. **Zero introduced failures**: 30 are inherited fixture/expectation/provenance failures; two are environment-related runner failures also present on the parent. PR180 repaired the parent's additional history fingerprint failure. The two environment cases pass under the separately recorded UTC/experimental-VM diagnostic control; the standard gate was not changed.

Broader integration is **257/261**. Its four additional inherited fixture failures reproduce on both prior PR180 and PR179 and are listed separately in the inventory, not folded into the standard 32.

Real PostgreSQL contention/pool-pressure qualification is unrun: no local PostgreSQL server/container toolchain is installed. Production SQL/lease fault models and canonical memory timing passed. The fence linearizes response construction against suppression; physical socket delivery and atomicity with independent Core writes are not claimed.

## Exact source and audit receipts

- Backend fix: `1aa5c66e9283024e78ad6f26f5450cbc61a37659`; evidence/report head: `a1876afaeaa59d9da47729487d490cba8cfc9d9c`.
- Paired frontend fix: `d626bb080d7774ba5fc8167661d21893d9f1e3c8`; evidence/report head: `5c784e3e46114816ba57db17ad7a2c2013a8d81a`.
- [Updated backend audit report](https://github.com/neo-capiro/meri-greenfield/blob/a1876afaeaa59d9da47729487d490cba8cfc9d9c/docs/integration/AUDIT-REPAIR-REVIEW-20261018.md)
- [Updated frontend audit report](https://github.com/neo-capiro/capiro-frontend/blob/5c784e3e46114816ba57db17ad7a2c2013a8d81a/docs/coordination/reports/AUDIT-CHAT-RENEWAL-20261018.md)

GitHub API publication recreates metadata; complete trees match the reviewed local commits recorded in both reports.

- Repair synthetic action receipts/routes/envelopes and canonical worker initial-input allocation, reaching the unchanged receiver, SDK and settlement assertions.
- Update six stale expectations only after checking accepted descriptor/package/route contracts; make the browser isolation test invoke its bounded VM child explicitly.
- Audit and refresh only the initial-input PostgreSQL provenance fingerprint; emitted browser code, schema and declarations stay byte-identical.
- Fix host-dependent UTC query-date normalization while preserving explicit-zone instants and invalid-input refusals; add cross-timezone and offset/comment coverage.

## Scope

Source-only follow-up to #180 (`a1876afa`). The whole-response retention fence borrowed a second PostgreSQL lease for its final watermarked read while holding the first lease for subject locks. A pool at capacity one queued that checkout until the release deadline. This branch uses a callback-scoped projection reader on the held lease, retains shared recovery exclusion through synchronous response serialization, and restricts reads to locked subjects before lease release. PR180 and PR175 owner branches are untouched.

The history service uses the scoped retention assertion only during its final release. The ordinary gate, suppression owner, joined projection/watermark statement, external ledger-head proof, source generator and scheduled-history custody routing remain in their canonical owners.

## Evidence

- Parent `a1876afa`: both max-one and concurrent max-two canonical history regressions failed with `CONVERSATION_UNAVAILABLE` from queued pool checkout.
- This branch: focused five-file run **112/112** (history, product release, retention release, scheduled history, history-source contract). New coverage includes one- and two-lease pools, suppression order, denied authorization cleanup, scoped subject/lifetime, and scheduled immutable occurrence custody.
- History-only generated metadata check, syntax and diff whitespace passed.
- The broader `postgres-watermark.test.mjs` run was **13/14**: its independently inventoried PR179/PR180 synthetic fixture at line 50 omits required `withTransition` and raises `RETENTION_CONFIGURATION`; other atomic snapshot checks passed. Standard PR180 release baseline (32 failing tests, runtime TypeScript 3, control TypeScript 18) is not qualified by this focused result.

prs.body:
## Exact base and ownership

Source successor to #180 at `a1876afaeaa59d9da47729487d490cba8cfc9d9c`. This branch changes only the canonical native usage parser and focused offline tests. It does not edit #180, frozen #175, or the separate pool, membership, model-alias and release-manifest branches.

## Repair

The stream parser requires a bound `message_start` input count and final cumulative `message_delta` output count before a terminal `message_stop` can yield `COMPLETE` usage data. Bedrock's `amazon-bedrock-invocationMetrics` stop extension is optional in the pinned LiteLLM decoder; when present, the parser validates its closed input/output/latency shape and requires its counts to match the bound CountTokens input and final delta output. Malformed or conflicting metrics stay sticky `UNKNOWN`. Optional cache read/write counts can only be zero. A present raw `message_stop.usage` is explicitly held `UNKNOWN` pending an exact provider fixture; it is not silently ignored. The existing event ordering, complete AWS frame/transport EOF, cancellation, raw evidence hash, reservation and final authorization boundaries remain in their canonical owners. Cache use is not priced as ordinary input.

The response and product callback regressions exercise one counted request, one reservation, one native send and one settlement with both a valid metrics extension and a bare terminal stop. Missing required start/delta usage, malformed or conflicting metrics, and truncated frames suppress the final successful body. Lost settlement acknowledgement uses one committed readback and retains failure if readback is unresolved.

## Checks and limits

- Credential-free focused Python run with the local pinned `botocore 1.43.111`, `httpx 0.28.1` and `LiteLLM 1.104.2` environment: **62/62 passed** across native usage, response settlement, host observation/composition and callback tests.
- `git diff --check` passed. Independent read-only review challenged the previous mandatory-metrics invariant and supported this optional-metrics correction.
- A direct import of the pinned LiteLLM 1.104.2 Bedrock decoder converted the documented terminal metrics to Anthropic-style usage. The full upstream streaming test did **not** run: the local diagnostic venv lacks FastAPI. No SDK/CLI, provider, AWS, live SQL, image build or deployment was run.

The [Anthropic streaming contract](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming) documents a bare stop after cumulative delta usage, while [AWS's illustrated terminal metrics](https://aws.amazon.com/cn/blogs/china/amazon-bedrock-monitoring-logging-practices/) are an example, not a guarantee for Sonnet 4.6. [Bedrock implicit caching](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html) means missing cache counters alone do not prove a live request was uncached. The exact Sonnet 4.6 raw stream and billing behavior, and broader model, history and Core authorization gates, remain unqualified. This source PR does not release those holds.

## Scope

Source-only control startup trust proposal stacked on PR #175 (`993f52a97e5d9edcf65c9f89423c097aa52831c7`). Control material initialization writes a verified CA bundle containing the unchanged locked 114-certificate RDS roots and the pinned private server CA. The control process reads that file through `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` before startup. The new bundle is private to the task, and hostname verification remains enabled.

## Focused verification

- 40 passed, 0 failed, 1 existing Linux-only skip with Node 22.23.3 on Windows.
- Synthetic loopback TLS: the RDS-only bundle rejects the private issuer; the combined bundle accepts the pinned private origin; a wrong hostname still fails.
- Independent source review found no blocking security or rollback issue.

## Held before any deployment

- Neo's startup audit and deployment/chat hold remain in force. This PR changes source only; no task definition, live resource, SQL, credential, IAM, network, model call, or chat was changed.
- Native Linux/Fargate IO and Node 24 are not verified here. Two renderer/Stage 3 fixture cases could not start because the local Python environment lacks `cryptography`.
- The live failure's exact TLS exception is unobserved, so this is a trust candidate, not proof of causality.
